title: Webb peers behind bars
caption: The barred spiral galaxy NGC 5068, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 5068 · constellation Virgo · about 17 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA & CSA, J. Lee and the PHANGS-JWST Team

recognition.text: ESA/Webb Picture of the Month (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Thousands upon thousands of tiny stars fill this close-up of a spiral galaxy, crowded most densely in a whitish bar at its core. Clumps and threads of dust form an almost skeletal framework that follows the twist of a spiral arm, and large glowing bubbles of red gas are tucked into the dust. This is NGC 5068, a barred spiral about 17 million light-years away in Virgo, with its bar in the upper left.

Stars and planets are born inside clouds of gas and dust that block visible light. Webb's MIRI and NIRCam instruments see in infrared, letting astronomers look straight through the dust of NGC 5068 and watch star formation as it happens.

This portrait is part of a campaign to build a treasure trove of star-formation observations in nearby galaxies. Star formation matters across astronomy, from the thin plasma between stars to the growth of whole galaxies.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (3.70 x 2.15 arcminutes) and distance (17 million light years), the frame spans roughly 18,000 × 11,000 light-years. Its light set out about 17 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image combines Webb's NIRCam and MIRI. Light at 2.0 micrometres is blue; 3.0 and 7.7 micrometres cyan; 3.35 and 10 micrometres green; 11 micrometres orange; and 3.6 and 21 micrometres red.
understand.eye: All of this is infrared light, invisible to the eye, and it passes through dust that would hide these regions in visible light.

explore: Webb imaged 19 nearby star-forming galaxies for the project. Astronomers combine them with Hubble catalogues of 10 000 star clusters, VLT maps of 20 000 star-forming nebulae, and ALMA observations of 12 000 dark, dense molecular clouds.
alt: A close-up of a spiral galaxy with a dense whitish bar of stars, skeletal clumps and filaments of dust along a spiral arm, and glowing red gas bubbles.
